summary:
### TL;DR
- No GitHub Changelog entries in this period.
- The only notable change is a rewrite of the enterprise GitHub Actions migration guide, now at a new URL under the Actions tutorials section. ([commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/bb615bcf16807083bad6ffe988864a5d5a061885))
- The new guide focuses on AI-assisted, wave-based migration from Jenkins, Azure DevOps, GitLab CI/CD, or CircleCI. ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/migrate-to-github-actions/migrate-an-enterprise))
- There are no breaking changes, deprecations, or security updates.

### Action required
Nothing this time.

Old URLs for the enterprise migration guide (under `/admin/...` and `/enterprise-onboarding/...`) redirect to the new page. Updating internal links is optional. ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/migrate-to-github-actions/migrate-an-enterprise))

### Security improvements
Nothing this time.

### Docs changes worth reading
- **New page: "Migrating your enterprise to GitHub Actions"** ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/migrate-to-github-actions/migrate-an-enterprise), [commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/bb615bcf16807083bad6ffe988864a5d5a061885))
  - The guide was moved from the admin/enterprise-onboarding docs to `actions/tutorials/migrate-to-github-actions/`. It applies to Free/Pro/Team, GHEC, and GHES.
  - It is aimed at administrators migrating many pipelines from Jenkins, Azure DevOps, GitLab CI/CD, or CircleCI.
  - It now frames migration as an AI-assisted process run in waves, "without disrupting delivery." It aims to produce:
    - a target design that improves on the current setup
    - a live inventory of which repos use which CI/CD system and how far each has migrated
    - a pilot group plus plans for later waves
    - AI tooling to convert pipeline syntax to your organization's standards
    - a plan to retire the old CI/CD system
  - The guide references an `actions-migrations-via-copilot` resource. The provided diff is truncated at that point, so details about that tooling aren't available here.
  - **Security note:** teams using AI-assisted pipeline conversion should review the generated workflows before adopting them. Check `permissions`, secret handling, and third-party action pinning.
- **Migration tutorials index updated:** the new "Migrate an enterprise" page is listed first, ahead of the automated and manual migration pages. ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/migrate-to-github-actions))

+## Introduction
+
+This guide is for administrators who are migrating many pipelines from an existing CI/CD system, such as Jenkins, Azure DevOps, GitLab CI/CD, or CircleCI, to {% data variables.product.prodname_actions %}.
+
+By the end of this guide, you'll have:
+
+* A target design that improves on your current setup
+* A live inventory of which repositories use which CI/CD system, and how far each one has migrated
+* A pilot migration group and a plan for future migration waves
+* AI tooling for converting pipeline syntax to your organization's standards
+* A plan for retiring the old CI/CD system
